vision: A standalone, headless Decimal engine for leveraged-crypto portfolio decisions — position sizing, liquidation, DCA, funding, hedging, fees, portfolio margin, stress, and options risk — consumed by TradingDashboard instead of reimplementing the math.

calc_primitives.description: New pure-Decimal calc primitives the TradingDashboard rebuild's future roadmap needs — hedging engine, per-account/concentration metrics, options + margin-bridge math, funding math. calculators.description: Port the pure risk/hedging calculators out of the retired TradingDashboard app into DeltaCalc.*

consumer_math.description: Pure-Decimal decision and aggregation primitives consumed at trading call sites: PnL/breakeven, net-delta hedging, portfolio-margin liquidation, stress scenarios, fees, funding carry, and explicit base-numeraire exposure/coverage. Inputs are caller-owned state plus provider facts; policy, I/O, and option pricing stay outside DeltaCalc.

contract_hardening.description: Cross-module correctness, input/output contracts, independent reference tests, and architecture work that makes the calculation surface trustworthy without adding I/O or portfolio policy.

task.body:
Audit-surfaced bug (Codex second-opinion, audit pass on 0da3fcf..HEAD; see .audit/bb6175c.md).

`DeltaCalc.Funding.compare_single_symbol/2` selects `max_exchange`/`min_exchange`, `delta`, and the `arbitrage_opportunity` flag from RAW per-period funding rates, but `annual_apr_delta/5` then annualizes each venue at its OWN cadence (`periods_per_day_for(venue)`) and subtracts. When venues have different cadences (the `%{venue => periods}` form introduced by task 28), the annualized spread can come out NEGATIVE and the venue labels invert.

Specific trigger:
  Funding.compare_funding_rates(
    %{hourly: Decimal.new("0.0001"), eight_hour: Decimal.new("0.0007")},
    %{hourly: 24, eight_hour: 3}
  )
ranks :eight_hour as max by raw rate (0.0007 > 0.0001), then annual_apr_delta = (0.0007*3*365*100) - (0.0001*24*365*100) = 76.65 - 87.60 = -10.95 — even though the hourly venue has the HIGHER annualized rate (87.60% vs 76.65%). max_exchange/min_exchange are mislabeled and the APR delta is negative/nonsensical.

The deeper question is a domain decision: `@arbitrage_threshold 0.0005` is a raw per-period value with no defined meaning across cadences. Decide whether cross-cadence ranking + arbitrage detection should operate on annualized (or per-day-normalized) rates throughout, and what the threshold becomes in those units. Same-cadence (scalar periods_per_day) behavior must stay unchanged — raw and annualized ranking agree when the cadence is constant, so only the mixed-cadence path changes.

Add a property/unit test for the mixed-cadence ranking inversion so coverage no longer ratifies the bug.

task.body:
`Funding.compare_funding_rates/2` now returns a `:delta` whose unit depends on the SHAPE of the `periods_per_day` argument: a scalar cadence yields a raw per-period spread (e.g. `0.002`), while a `%{venue => periods}` map yields a per-day-normalized spread (e.g. `0.0003`). This is documented in the `@doc` and intentional, but it leaks into `find_arbitrage_opportunities/2`, whose default `min_delta` (`0.001`) was tuned for the raw per-period scale. Mixed-cadence comparison maps are filtered against a threshold ~3x too large, so genuine daily-normalized spreads can be silently dropped, and a caller cannot mix scalar- and map-derived comparison results in one `find_arbitrage_opportunities` call without scale skew.

Decide the domain-correct contract: either (a) make `:delta` a single consistent unit across both paths and adjust `annual_apr_delta` accordingly, or (b) keep dual units but make `find_arbitrage_opportunities` cadence-aware (normalize its `min_delta`, or read a unit tag off the comparison entry). Whichever path, document the chosen unit on the `:delta` field and cover it with a test that runs a map-cadence comparison through `find_arbitrage_opportunities`.

task.title: Fix inverted min_delta raw→daily scaling in Funding.find_arbitrage_opportunities (divide vs multiply)
acceptance_criteria: find_arbitrage_opportunities raw→daily min_delta scaling matches the file's own arbitrage-threshold convention (raw threshold × periods_per_day to reach daily terms), or a documented justification is given for why min_delta diverges
A raw per-period spread strictly below min_delta is excluded after daily normalization; one at/above is included — proven by a worked dimensional example in the test, not re-asserting current output
The task-36 golden test 'normalizes min_delta for venue-cadence-map comparison entries' is re-derived from first principles, not from the inverted scaling

Remove the `@tag :domain_pending` from the task-37 raw→daily scaling test in test/delta_calc/domain_invariants_test.exs so the invariant runs green under mix ci
out_of_scope: Changing the arbitrage threshold domain constant (@arbitrage_threshold) itself
Changing the :delta unit tagging contract introduced by task 36
Adding new venue cadence presets
task.body:
Task 36 added `threshold_for_delta_unit/2` so `find_arbitrage_opportunities/2` filters `:daily_normalized` comparison entries against a cadence-aware threshold. The scaling DIRECTION appears inverted. For `:daily_normalized` entries it computes `min_delta / @default_periods_per_day` (divide by 3), but the daily delta is `raw_rate * periods_per_day` — LARGER than a raw per-period spread, not smaller. To express a raw per-period `min_delta` on the same daily basis as the delta it is compared against, it should be MULTIPLIED by periods, not divided.

The decisive internal evidence: the SAME daily code path normalizes its arbitrage gate raw→daily by MULTIPLYING — `@mixed_cadence_arbitrage_threshold = @arbitrage_threshold * @default_periods_per_day` (0.0005 * 3 = 0.0015), with a docstring that explicitly calls this "the default 8-hour raw threshold normalized to daily terms". So the file uses ×periods for one raw→daily conversion (arbitrage threshold) and ÷periods for the other (min_delta) — contradictory directions for the identical conversion. Consequence: daily-normalized entries pass `min_delta` filtering ~9x more permissively than intended, the opposite of "filter scalar- and map-cadence results together without scale skew".

Root cause to watch for: task 36's own body framed the original bug as "filtered against a threshold ~3x too large, so genuine daily-normalized spreads can be silently dropped" and illustrated the map delta as `0.0003` (smaller than raw) — both dimensionally backwards, since daily = raw × periods is larger. The implementer faithfully encoded the backwards premise, and the golden test (`normalizes min_delta for venue-cadence-map comparison entries`, min_delta 0.0045 → threshold 0.0015) was computed WITH the inverted scaling, so coverage ratifies it. Re-derive the threshold from dimensional analysis, not from the existing golden.

Verify against the daily path's arbitrage threshold convention and a worked example: a raw per-period spread below `min_delta` must NOT pass once normalized to daily, and one at/above must. Pure Decimal, no I/O. Scalar-cadence (`:raw_per_period`) filtering must remain unchanged.

task.title: Add base-numeraire inverse exposure and covered-call coverage math
acceptance_criteria: Pure Decimal APIs return separately named base-numeraire exposure, settlement coverage, and risk-target results; coverage never implies delta neutrality or approval, and a fully covered position with non-zero residual delta remains outside an explicit neutral target

Option exposure requires a semantic tag distinguishing Black-Scholes delta from provider-supplied Net Transaction Delta: Black-Scholes delta subtracts the option mark exactly once, while Net Transaction Delta is never adjusted a second time
Option quantity requires a unit tag distinguishing base-currency amount from contract count; contract count is multiplied exactly once by a caller-supplied base-currency contract size

Golden tests pin the Black-Scholes case delta = 0.40 base and option mark = 0.05 base: signed base amount +1 returns +0.35 base and -1 returns -0.35 base; a base-denominated mark is not divided by spot and a quote-denominated mark is converted once

Inverse-perpetual inputs distinguish signed USD notional from signed contract count: USD notional divides by mark once, while contract count multiplies by caller-supplied USD contract size before dividing by mark; independent long and short fixtures pin both shapes

Settlement-period input is either tagged provider-adjusted Net Transaction Delta or explicitly tagged decayed delta and mark components; ambiguous settlement input is rejected rather than passed through the ordinary formula
Covered-call coverage reports eligible base, disjoint existing reservations, proposed obligation, remaining capacity, and uncovered amount without inferring portfolio identity
Unsupported, untagged, or mixed unit shapes return a named error; every public function is Descripex-advertised and Decimal-valued

Computing Black-Scholes Greeks or deriving settlement decay from a clock
Portfolio persistence, reservation ownership/deduplication, approval policy, UI, alerts, strategy selection, or roll scheduling
Order submission, reconciliation, and venue margin preflight
Base-numeraire gamma, vega, or theta transformation

Add the pure calculation boundary needed by an ETH-numeraire covered-call portfolio. Keep two
questions orthogonal: (1) settlement coverage — whether eligible base inventory covers the maximum
base obligation of existing and proposed short calls; and (2) numeraire risk — the signed local
exposure and whether it satisfies a caller-supplied target. A covered call can still carry material
delta, so coverage must never waive a hedge/risk target or produce an approval decision.

Deribit's provider-owned contract defines Net Transaction Delta as Black-Scholes delta minus option
mark price. Therefore tag which semantic the caller supplies: apply the subtraction once to a
Black-Scholes delta, and never subtract the mark from an already adjusted Net Transaction Delta.
Also tag option quantity as base-currency amount or contract count. Deribit documents option amount
and option contract size in base currency, so a contract count must multiply by the supplied base
contract size exactly once. A base-denominated mark is not divided by spot; a quote-denominated mark
is converted once.

For inverse perpetuals, distinguish a signed USD-notional input from a signed contract-count input.
USD notional converts to base once by dividing by mark; contract count first multiplies by the
caller-supplied USD contract size and then divides by mark. Untagged or mixed shapes fail rather than
guessing whether an exchange `amount` means contracts or USD. Prove both directions with independent
hand-calculated fixtures and no venue constants.

During Deribit settlement, option delta and mark decay toward intrinsic settlement values. Accept
either provider-adjusted Net Transaction Delta or explicitly tagged decayed components; do not apply
the ordinary formula to an ambiguous settlement-period value.

Coverage consumes already-classified, mutually exclusive quantities: eligible base inventory,
existing short-call obligations, pending/open sell reservations, other reservations, and the
proposed short-call amount. DeltaCalc performs Decimal arithmetic and reports capacity/uncovered
amount; the consumer owns identities, persistence, double-spend prevention, policy, and approval.

task.title: Align single-position liquidation price with the venue cross-margin formula
acceptance_criteria: liquidation/4 returns entry * (1 - 1/leff) / (1 - mmr_total) for :long and entry * (1 + 1/leff) / (1 + mmr_total) for :short; the fixture entry 2279, leff 3, mmr_total 0.021 yields long 1551.93 and short 2976.16 to the cent

Golden fixtures are hand-derived from Hyperliquid's published liquidation formula with explicit account_value, position_size, and maintenance ratio inputs, and cross-checked against a second venue's published formula; both source URLs and the derivation are in the test
A property test pins long liquidation < entry < short liquidation for leff > 1, that both move toward entry as leff grows, and that raising mmr_total moves both toward entry
An unreachable long liquidation (leff <= 1) still returns zero, with a test naming that contract

out_of_scope: Netted-book liquidation in DeltaCalc.PortfolioMargin (already uses the venue-equivalent numerator/denominator form)
Venue-specific tiered maintenance schedules; mmr_total stays a caller-supplied value
Changing the return shape to nil or an error for unreachable liquidation
Consumer changes in trading_dashboard
task.body:
`DeltaCalc.Liquidation.liquidation/4` prices a single position's liquidation as
`factor = (1 - mmr_total) / leff`, `long = entry * (1 - factor)`, `short = entry * (1 + factor)`
(read 2026-09-16, lib/delta_calc/liquidation.ex). That divides the maintenance margin by the
leverage, which no venue does. Hyperliquid's published formula
(https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/liquidations, fetched 2026-09-16):
`liq_price = price - side * margin_available / position_size / (1 - l * side)` with
`l = 1 / MAINTENANCE_LEVERAGE` (the maintenance margin ratio) and, for cross margin,
`margin_available = account_value - maintenance_margin_required`. For one position with
equity E, notional N = leff * E and mmr l, that reduces to
`long = entry * (1 - 1/leff) / (1 - l)` and `short = entry * (1 + 1/leff) / (1 + l)`.

Worked numbers at entry 2279, leff 3, mmr_total 0.021: current long 1535.29 vs venue 1551.93

The 2026-09-16 post-merge audit of 3b3e4d5..9732c4d (task 56) verified that all 14 remaining

required — and found that the elision rule is coarser than it looks. `elided?/1` is

including every concrete value documented alongside it.

Measured against the current README: the 14 elided examples document **57** key/value pairs, of
which **44 are concrete** (`final_avg_entry: #Decimal<2910.638297872340425531914893617022>`,
`daily_funding_rate: #Decimal<0.045>`, `periods_per_day: #Decimal<3>`,
`total_exposure: #Decimal<124500>`, `portfolio_margin: #Decimal<27.0000>`, ...) and unchecked by

scalars and task 56 closed the last two holdouts; this is the same hole one level deeper, and it
is the larger share — 44 unchecked documented values vs the 3 that tasks 55/56 fixed.

Those values are also the ones most likely to rot, because they are the multi-field decision maps
(`DCAPlanner`, `MarginBridge`, `StressScenario`, `PortfolioMargin`, `DeltaNeutral`) that phase-3
behavior changes actually move — the 2026-09-16 README audit found the liquidation-formula change
had already rotted several of them before task 55 landed.

documented structure and compare only the positions that are not `...`. Keep the whole-result path
byte-identical so task 55/56's guarantees do not regress, and keep a census (or equivalent) that
still distinguishes a *whole-result* elision from a partial one, so the quiet-opt-out guard task 55
built is not lost.

Secondary, same files, same session: three README results are asserted but 34 digits long
(`#Decimal<1507.537688442211055276381909547739>` is the first example a `Calc` reader sees). They
are not a correctness gap — the gate checks them — but they are the illegibility task 56 named, and
they are brittle against a `decimal` context-precision change (CLAUDE.md § Dependency Gotchas:
default went 28 -> 34 in decimal 3.x). Decide the convention once and apply it consistently rather
than leaving the README carrying both.

values become checked) and negative cases that prove the new path fails; no lib/ behavior involved.

Sibling check (DD-8): tasks 16 and 23 were flagged as sharing `modules` / `manifest`. Different
surface — both are *content* tasks that added v0_2 / v0_3 modules to `@modules` and the README so
the agent manifest advertises them. This task changes no registration and adds no module; it
hardens the *test-side detector* of invariant 6, which did not exist when 16/23 were written. The
real sibling is task 58, which landed that invariant and is `done`/shipped; this is the follow-up
its chosen scope left open, not a repeat instance of it.

Found by the 2026-09-16 post-merge audit of `6f870dc..3757dd5` (task 58).

Task 58 landed the doctest-registration invariant scoped to `Manifest.modules()`, which its
acceptance criteria explicitly allowed. That scope is sound because invariant 5 forces every
publicly documented `lib/delta_calc/` module into `@modules` — with exactly two carve-outs:

  * `DeltaCalc` lives at `lib/delta_calc.ex`, outside the `lib/delta_calc/` directory
    `documented_modules_from_lib/0` scans, and is not in `@modules`. It happens to be covered
    today only because `test/delta_calc_test.exs` carries a `doctest DeltaCalc` that currently
    registers zero examples (the suite reports 2 doctests, both `FundingProjection`'s).
  * `DeltaCalc.Manifest` is `Enum.reject`ed by name in `documented_modules_from_lib/0`, so it is
    documented, ungated by invariant 5, and ungated by invariant 6.

So an `iex>` example added to the library's front-door moduledoc or to `Manifest`'s is not
covered by the gate that exists to catch exactly that. The hole is narrow, but it is on the two
most-read modules in the package.

The two halves of the fix are coupled and must land together: widening the gated set while the
detector stays `String.contains?(doc, "iex>")` turns CI red immediately, because task 58's own
sixth-invariant line in `DeltaCalc.Manifest`'s `@moduledoc` — "Every registered module whose
compiled docs contain `iex>` examples ..." — is a prose mention that the substring test cannot
distinguish from an example. Anchoring the match to an example line resolves both.

Note the detector's error direction is currently safe: a prose mention can produce a spurious
failure, never a silent pass, so nothing that landed is under-enforced. This is hardening, not a
correctness bug.

Sibling check (DD-8): task 59 [done] shares `gate` / `manifest`. This is deliberately NOT a third
instance of 59's class — it is the class statement 59's chosen scope left unwritten. Task 59 named
two specific ungated modules and added them to the gate by hand; this task removes the hand, so a
third instance cannot be filed. Per the DD-8 rule that is the "widen to the class" resolution
rather than the "don't file the instance" one, and it needs its own task because it changes gate
logic and adds a derivation test — work outside the doc-drift scope of the audit that found it.

Found by the 2026-09-16 post-merge audit of `2cc5071..fc39c8b` (task 59).

Task 59 closed the two known holes in the doctest-registration invariant by widening its set to
`[DeltaCalc, Manifest | Manifest.modules()]`. That is correct for the tree as it stands, but it
replaces a derived set with a literal carve-out list — the exact shape task 58's own CHANGELOG
entry claims the gate avoids ("never from a hand-maintained allowlist"). Two latent holes remain,
both silent passes rather than spurious failures:

  * `documented_modules_from_lib/0` calls `File.ls!` on `lib/delta_calc/`, which is not
    recursive. `lib/` is flat today, so nothing is missed — but the first module placed in a
    subdirectory is invisible to invariant 5 (registration) *and*, transitively, to invariant 6.
  * A new documented module added at `lib/*.ex` alongside `delta_calc.ex` is outside the scanned
    directory and absent from the literal, so it is gated by neither invariant until someone
    remembers to extend the list.

Neither is a correctness bug in what has landed; both are the gate failing open on a shape the
library does not have yet. The fix is to derive the set the gate walks from the filesystem, which
also removes the carve-out list as a thing that must be maintained in step with `lib/`.
